title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus in Banach Spaces

problemStatement.formal: \int_a^b f = F(b)-F(a) \text{ and } \frac{d}{dx}\int_a^x f = f(x) \text{ for Banach-space-valued functions}
problemStatement.plain: Lift the fundamental theorem of calculus from real-valued functions to Banach-space-valued functions, with clean wrappers for both FTC directions and product/pi-space examples.
whyMatters: Banach-space FTC statements show that the calculus API is genuinely reusable beyond scalar real functions.
The file gives compact wrappers around Mathlib's general integral and derivative infrastructure.

proven: `ftc2_banach` and `ftc2_banach_general` prove the evaluation form of FTC for Banach-space-valued functions.
`banach_antiderivatives_differ_by_constant` records uniqueness of antiderivatives up to constants.
`ftc2_product` and `ftc2_pi` give concrete product and finite-dimensional examples.
`ftc_banach_summary` collects the main Banach-space FTC facts.
open: Related Lebesgue and Stokes FTC files still contain axioms or sorries; this OQ04 Banach-space file itself records zero axioms and zero sorries.
knownResults.goal: Use the completed Banach-space wrappers as a clean bridge from scalar FTC to vector-valued integration.
